extra.message: User-supplied `username` query parameter is interpolated directly into a SQL string at `/select` and passed to `cursor.execute()`. This allows SQL injection (e.g., `?username=\" OR 1=1; -- `) to read or modify data.

User-supplied fields from the `User` request body are interpolated into an INSERT statement in the `/user` PUT endpoint. Quotes are not escaped, so any field (name, username, address, email, contact, or password hash) can be used to inject SQL.
User-supplied `username` query parameter is interpolated directly into a DELETE statement at `/user`, allowing SQL injection and arbitrary record deletion or data manipulation.
The `address` field from the optional `User` request body is interpolated unquoted into a DELETE statement at `/user`, enabling SQL injection.

The `/find` POST endpoint reads arbitrary JSON from the request body and passes it directly to `users.find(query)`. Attackers can supply MongoDB-style operators (e.g., `{"id": {"$in": [1,2]}}`) to query arbitrary documents.

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic

extra.message: The `/reset` POST endpoint deletes the SQL and NoSQL database files and reinitializes the database without any authentication or authorization checks, allowing any unauthenticated user to destroy all application data.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: The `/user` DELETE endpoint removes records from both the NoSQL and SQL databases based on user-supplied `username` or `User.address` without any authentication or authorization checks.

extra.message: When `run_sql_query()` returns more than one row it returns the raw SQL tuples in `{'users': _data}`, including the `password` column (MD5 hash). This exposes password hashes to API consumers.
